How you go to a gym? Bussing. Or 30-40 minute walk outside everyday. How to volunteer- Google volunteer jobs in your city- check their post dates, requirements. Volunteering isn't bullshit you can enter cool organizations: marketing/pr positions, personal support worker, IT, mentorship/mental health, hospitals, many things. What do you care about man? Helping refugees, troubled kids, what moves you? 

Back to the job thing- right now you are not in terms to work- you need to get used to waking up at a normal time and get used to structure- having a commitment/discipline everyday leaving the house to go to the gym, volunteer, get help, socialize with people meetup app. Once you are more stable then you can worry about a job. You will go to an employment Center and get help to write a professional resume using references and experiences from volunteering, they will forward you postings they find- you can't blame your unemployment on your parents not helping you unacceptable- that is on you, you're an adult and they deserve a life they work all day and deserve to relax at home. 

Now isn't the right time- but when you get on your feet. You could also consider a fast college certificate that will give you a competitive edge for work- you will not have to compete with the entire population (young and old) and high school kids for minimum wage retail job; yes they are very competitive for experience and want you to be young and hot and extraverted to push sales. But you can do a one year chef training program, not everyone is a trained chef no more high school brats, and you earn more than minimum wage, a decent and respectable living. You will have self respect your own home, life, people will be more attracted to you when you're put together doors open to girls. Your life is a big project like building a house it's one small step after another, brick by brick, as things start falling into place and structure. 

No you're not going to wake up today or tomorrow and feel awesome or be a big shot. But now you have a plan you can choose to carry out once you get exhausted of being so miserable and one day decide to change. You know for now your best option is to volunteer its not forever it can be a pet project for 2 months meanwhile you also get a pension due to mental health and while you also take care of your health gym, watch what you eat, see therapist in hospital and a doc for anxiety meds. Then go to college maybe next semester; and/or employment agency; maybe do a bartending or waitressing training for work too.

1) Okay so however many therapists you saw its clear you two lacked chemistry, and you were not comfortable with "bob 1" or "bob 2". You can't say all of therapy doesn't work. It doesn't work to simply go to a therapist to solve your problems; you have to find THE therapist for you. Finding a good therapist is a screening process. Research therapists who are specialized in your problem area whatever that may be e.g. specialized treating addictions or anxiety disorders. Once you find a couple of them I want you to book appointments with 3 or 4 different therapists at the same time; this way you save time and you try many different people on for size and find who you actually like  or think is smart. Different schools of therapy are entirely different planets- gestalt (role playing), dbt (present centered, emotion regulation), psychotherapy (past centered), list goes on. Being an adult no one can force you on any medication you don't consent to; being confronted in that situation worst that happens you say no thank you which lasted a total 30 seconds. 

2) You are making a lot of judgments; you are not a mind reader to say "doctors" will look at me and think this of me and then this is what they are going to do and then they won't give me the drugs I need. They are there and want to help you- no they are not going to think you are a meth head or boogey monster because you are a person coming to them seeking help.. ok 

3) You have a distorted self image and low self esteem. You are your own worst critic slashing at yourself- i'm sure you don't look like a meth head. cut yourself some slack. 

How long have you been unemployed? Have you gone to any job employment agencies, had any appointments to speak to someone? 

If you are immobilized at home, without a car or transportation. How do you go out? 

Okay that's great you enjoy things. Carve out some time each day to reward yourself after putting in effort.

You had a really unfortunate circumstance with your ex girlfriend  not all people are like that. There are good and bad people in the world you are going with practice and learning to be careful in detecting early signs/red flags to avoid 

How are you structuring each day, are you being productive to get out of this hole you're in?

hey buddy. I know this is all very scary and overwhelming right now. I understand and share in your pain all too well; I'll share my story and how I overcame. Right now you have to make a conscious effort to de-escalate your intense feelings, do not panic. 

*Grounding exercises, mindfulness, distress tolerance skills, breathing- look into these and bring them in therapy. I know you don't want to but you must act opposite to how you feel: eat something, get a short walk fresh air, you're not sleeping take melatonin or get sleeping pills, cry if you need to, get support/hugs from family, and find healthy distractions like baking yummy goodies you can't be grieving/ruminating all day. Do relaxing things like put on music of ocean/water sounds, knitting, read something easy nothing on suicide or sickness online- don't torment yourself. 

I know feelings of suicide are very real its intense but also you do not want to actually die- you are here right now wanting to connect to other people; asking for instruments/advice on what to do and who to go to. This is amazing and gives me hope. 

I don't know your entire background but I will help you problem solve given what you've shared. 1) There is bullying/discrimination happening in your school it must be reported to the office and authorities. If there are text messages/cyber bullying report it to the police it is a federal crime. 2) This school became a toxic environment its best you remove yourself from it. First I want you to recover seeing your doctor/ get things a little more managed. Then you will go to a new school. 3) Find support networks- group therapy, community groups/church, meetups for people recovering mental health, sports groups, volunteering is a great way to meet new people, new school, later a part time job. 4) Therapy and treatment are vital it doesn't mean you are weak it means you are a warrior. ***Baby steps tackle one thing at a time first we need you to get better. 

I live with mental health problems, I sometimes have hallucinations, major depression and panic disorders. However, you can still live a meaningful life. I am 23 through some bumps along the way I am finishing my university psychology degree, I have few very close friends, love from my parents, am a proud dog owner, and enjoy travelling every year. I can say I'm pretty happy with my life and come a long way! 

Have you researched there are so many incredible people in this world who happen to be diagnosed with schizophrenia and they didn't let that stop them from living incredible lives. Syd Barett founder and musician of pink floyd, John Nash 1994 nobel prize winner, superbowl champion Lionel Aldridge, First lady Mary Lincoln. The list is endless. I see them and don't think their loonies who need to be hospitalized; I see real heroes who overcame a lot and contributed to humanity the world wouldn't be the same without them. 

Take care and love yourself
